newsitem.title: USA: US debt portfolios grow more defensive - survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt portfolios grow more defensive - survey.

text.p: Defensive changes in money managers' U.S. debt portfolios were moderate but pronounced in the week ended September 10, said a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"Despite the post-data rally on Friday, money managers appeared to have shortened duration exposure and become somewhat more defensive since the August employment report," the report said.
The report said the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading jumped to 4.14 from 4.04 the week before, while the asset-weighted number came in at 4.08, down from the 4.34 in the previous period.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio rose to 7.31 percent from 6.72 percent.
Duration bogey held steady at 4.06 on an arithmetic basis and 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

None of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, sharply down from 28 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those who intend to be active was not available; last week the number was 5.14.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
